definition: Illusion — in Kashmir Śaivism, māyā is not the world (as in Advaita) but the power by which Śiva limits himself, creating the appearance of difference and finitude. Māyā is Śiva's own power, not an independent reality.

sources.claim: māyā = standing-apart; not different from consciousness-nonduality, stands as other.

translations.note: Māyā = standing-apart; not different from consciousness-nonduality, stands as other. In Paramārthacarcā, Māyā is not cut off from its ground. (Paramārthacarcā v.4, Spandasandoha v.3)
